title: Idolatry
english: The things of God's glory are cast aside, and the nations are considered as nothing. If all nations are as nothing, to what likeness can God be compared? What image can be made of him, and what can be equal to him in weight, nature, or glory? Can it be through the crafts of a builder or the skills of a woodworker? Or is it as if formed into an image towards something of the creations? That is, was a human-like statue made? By no means, for nothing can be equal to God. God, being by nature and not being another, will surpass all things.

The worshipers of idols are in error, with no skill of building on the earth. But not even the handmade things would be saved if the craftsman had not wisely sought the means by which they could stand and have an unshaken foundation. As David says, 'The idols of the nations are silver and gold, the work of human hands' (Psalm 115:4).

All who engage in such practices and trust in them are like those who ridicule the construction of idols. By turning the discourse to shame and correction, the erring are shown the fault in this matter, and without excuse, the fault in this matter is revealed to them, saying: Do you not know? Do you not hear? Has it not been announced to you from the beginning? Do you not know the foundations of the earth, which are its last and furthest parts? Those who are from the ends to the ends have known, and they have heard, and it was announced to them from the beginning.

But what was announced? That God, the one by nature and truly, is one and only. In contrast, wood and stones, and nothing else, are made into gods by humans. The God-inspired Scripture has not been silent on this matter. The knowledge of truth has been proclaimed from above, through patriarchs, through the law and prophets. This proclamation occurred even before the only-begotten Word of God became human and appeared to those on earth, an event that marked the beginning of the deception of error. However, the accusation of idolatry was ancient, a fact that underscores the long history of this error.

title: The True Judgment Revealed in Christ
english: All those being initiated will hear the same message from the mystagogues. Speaking as moved by one Spirit, they do not argue with one another in words but instead harmoniously proclaim the divine doctrines. They announce the mystery of Christ covertly, as befits the sacred instruction of newcomers. This, I believe, is what was meant by 'Then they shall declare judgment.' For the people of Israel had named the law given through Moses as judgment, and thus it is quite reasonable that they would oppose the evangelical and saving proclamation by setting it against the law, calling this proclamation judgment through these very actions. For the true righteous judgment, and the power of the legislation that pleases God, is not more clearly seen in the shadow of the law, but shines forth in the proclamation of the holy mystagogues who are the new leaders. Those who have learned from Christ the judgment—that is, the will of God the Father—have proclaimed this same judgment to us by living in accordance with it. Who stirred up righteousness from the east? He summoned it to walk at his feet, and it goes forth. We ought not to marvel at the God who possesses all merely because of the mere greatness of his works, but also because of the benefits he bestows, through which he makes manifest his own tranquility. For he has saved those upon the earth, utterly destroyed the human race and death, brought forth corruption, and stripped the devil of his malicious abundance. He has abolished the devil's tyranny together with its powers, yet he has made known through faith the defeat of sin that once tyrannized over us, having put it to shame. Indeed, all these things have been set right through Christ.
follows the will of the Father more closely than anyone else, walking in perfect obedience and revealing the Father’s nature to all who believe.

title: Idolatry and Divine Knowledge
english: God says that the counsels of idolaters have drawn near, as King Jacob affirms, and He has well explained the calling of the nations in due time, promising to transform the desert into a forest and the dry land into waterways, complete with cedars, boxwood, and other plants, and to make His hand marvelous, saying, as the creator of such great things, He makes His hand marvelous by doing so.

By doing so, He addresses the makers of idols and such craftsmen, warning them that their judgment is near, which refers to the punishment owed to them, namely, shame and remorse, for by God's holy vote and just judgment, they would be punished as having deceived those under heaven and introduced untrue counsels.
They have taught people to speak to wood, saying, 'You are my father,' and to stone, 'You begot me' (Isaiah 44:24).

With these things, God says their counsels have drawn near, that is, have come to an end, as He dispels the deception and the mist of ignorance, and not one of their false names remains, but the Lord and God in truth, and the King of Jacob, that is, of those from the blood of Israel.

Through these things, He brings to remembrance the signs that have occurred, concerning the redemption of those from Israel, and through these signs, the power of His inherent divine authority is well known, or His unsurpassed superiority.
Let them draw near and promise what will happen to you, or what things were before; say, and we will set our mind and know what the last things and the things to come are (Isaiah 41:22-23).
Do good or evil, and we will marvel and see where you are from and what your work is, for you were chosen from the earth as an abomination.

It is characteristic of divine and ineffable glory to know everything and be ignorant of nothing, neither past nor present nor future, as it is written: 'Nothing will be hidden from me?' (Jeremiah 23:24).

This is evident in the words of the all-wise Moses, who described the creation of the world in detail, saying: 'In the beginning, God created the heaven and the earth' (Genesis 1:1), and our Lord Jesus Christ, who spoke through Moses, also announced to us the things in the end times, as His disciple says: 'We await new heavens and a new earth, and His promises' (2 Peter 3:13).
For the word of God is truly living and evident.
